  "description": "Expanded Series Bible III #2 You’re Not Who I Expected reusable adult idea source: an engine that generates premises where {{char}} knows {{user}} through reputation, online presence, mutual friends, a hobby community or rumours, then discovers the actual person does not match the assembled image — with mirrored variants where {{char}} is the one breaking expectations. Varies the source of the image, why the gap exists, which dimension it concerns, its polarity and what remains open afterwards.",
  "source_version": "1.0",

    "document": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible III",

  "summary": "{{char}} knows {{user}} first through reputation, online presence, work, mutual friends, a hobby community, rumours or second-hand stories, and then encounters the actual person the image was about. The engine is the collision between an assembled portrait and a real adult: the legend may be deflated, hidden depths revealed, or the surprise may fit neither pattern. The gap can concern appearance, social confidence, occupation, hobbies, temperament, lifestyle or values; the source may be accurate but incomplete, exaggerated, outdated or misinterpreted; the expectation may be positive or negative. Mirrored variants place {{char}} in the expectation-breaking role, and mutual variants give both characters wrong versions of each other. The reveal complicates an assumption rather than proving all public information fake, and what each person does with the correction remains open.",
  "core_premise": "An adult woman who has assembled a complete image of {{user}} from second-hand information — workplace reputation, online persona, mutual friends' stories, hobby community standing, rumours, family anecdotes, professional files or an ex's retelling — comes face to face with the actual person and finds the match imperfect in ways that matter. The image is not framed as a deception; it is what honest, exaggerated, outdated or simply misread information produces. The discovery may humble a legend, reveal hidden depths, or scramble the picture sideways, and mirrored variants run the same engine with {{user}} holding the mistaken image of {{char}}. Neither character is automatically rewarded for being more authentic, and whether the acquaintance deepens, cools, turns romantic or stays professional is undecided.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult discovery-drama opening. Establish what {{char}} believed about {{user}} and exactly where that belief came from — a traceable source such as a teller, thread, profile, incident or file — so the later collision has a history. Establish the occasion that puts the real {{user}} in front of her, the dimension along which he fails to match the image, and whether the expectation was flattering, unflattering or mixed. Give {{char}} her own occupation, friends, boundaries and reasons for caring about the mismatch. Begin at or near the moment the assembled picture first cracks, without writing {{user}}'s dialogue, feelings or reaction, and without deciding how the gap resolves.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Source of the expectation: workplace reputation, online presence, mutual friends' stories, hobby community standing, rumours, family anecdotes, professional files or second-hand retellings.",
    "Whether the reputation was accurate but incomplete, exaggerated, outdated, or simply misinterpreted.",

    "What remains open: whether the picture is updated, defended, discarded or replaced by something closer than either expected."

    "Keep ground truth separate from character rationalisation. A cheater may believe that omission was not lying, that getting caught was the only mistake, or that her relationship was already effectively over. Those are her beliefs, not narrator-endorsed facts.",

      "content": "The core engine is the collision between an assembled second-hand image of a person and the actual adult in front of {{char}}. Every card built from this source needs a real image, a real person, and a specific dimension along which they fail to match."
    },
    {
      "id": "reputation",
      "label": "Reputation",
      "content": "Establish where the image came from — a teller, thread, profile, incident, file or namesake that concretely exists. Decide whether the reputation was accurate but incomplete, exaggerated, outdated or misinterpreted, and whether the expectation was flattering, unflattering or mixed."
    },
    {
      "id": "reveal",
      "label": "Reveal",
      "content": "Choose the occasion that puts the real {{user}} in front of {{char}}: a planned meeting, workplace assignment, wedding, convention, emergency or accident. Open at or near the moment the picture first cracks, not years later, and let further information keep arriving."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap",
      "label": "Gap",
      "content": "The mismatch should be dimensional — appearance, confidence, occupation, hobbies, temperament, lifestyle, values, humour, money or communication — and specific rather than a vague aura. Several dimensions can disagree at once; attractiveness alone is a weak choice."
    },
    {
      "id": "polarity",
      "label": "Polarity",
      "content": "Decide whether the expectation was a legend to be deflated, an underdog with hidden depths, or a sideways surprise that fits neither. Do not treat deflation as punishment or revelation as reward; neither character is owed an arc."
    },
    {
      "id": "mirrored",
      "label": "Mirrored variants",
      "content": "The engine can run the other way: {{user}} holds the mistaken image of {{char}}. Apply identical rules — his image is his belief, not truth, and her actual self is not framed as a confession of fakery. Mutual double mismatches, where both were wrong about each other, are also valid."
    },
    {
      "id": "trigger",
      "label": "Trigger",

    },

      "id": "character",

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for You’re Not Who I Expected. {{char}} knows {{user}} only through second-hand information — workplace reputation, online persona, mutual friends' stories, hobby community standing, rumours, family anecdotes, a professional file, an ex's retelling or a matching profile — and then meets the actual person, who fails to match the image in a specific dimension: appearance, social confidence, occupation, hobbies, temperament, lifestyle, values, humour, money habits or communication style. Decide whether the image was accurate but incomplete, exaggerated, outdated or misinterpreted; whether the expectation was positive, negative or sideways; whether the reveal deflates a legend, uncovers hidden depths or scrambles the picture; and whether a mirrored variant instead gives {{user}} the mistaken image of {{char}}. The reveal complicates an assumption rather than proving everything public was fake; neither character is automatically rewarded for being more authentic. Open near the moment the picture cracks, with the source of the image traceable. Non-negotiables: all participants are adults; {{user}}'s feelings, reactions and future are never scripted; assumptions are beliefs, not objective truth; romance is never forced where discovery, friendship or rivalry fits better; consent, boundaries and every outcome remain open."
